sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Match Column A (personality trait) with Column B (feature). A: (a) Thinking (b) Feeling. B: (i) Prefer personal values (ii) Prefer to be structured (iii) Self-discipline and organised (iv) Use logic to handle problems.
Identify True or False. (a) Emotional stability is a personality trait listed under the Big Five model. (b) People with an intuition type personality are sociable and assertive.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: sociable and assertive people are extroverts.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) ________ is the act of conveying information for the purpose of creating mutual understanding. (b) ________ is an exchange of facts, ideas, opinions or emotions by two or more persons.
questions.answer: (a) Communication. (b) Communication (Newman and Summer's definition).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) People who are sociable, assertive and enjoy more frequent social interaction are called ________. (b) The tendency to experience unpleasant emotions easily such as anger, anxiety and depression is called ________.
questions.answer: (a) Extroverts. (b) Emotional instability (emotional stability trait).

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Communication is a process that involves at least two persons. (b) Oral communication does not provide immediate feedback.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it provides immediate feedback.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The three major factors that determine personality are heredity, environment and ________. (b) Tuckman's second stage of team development is ________.
questions.answer: (a) Situation. (b) Storming.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) A notice, agenda and minutes are the steps in convening a meeting. (b) Written communication provides immediate feedback.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it does not.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Agreeableness (b) Conscientiousness. B: (i) Compassionate and cooperative (ii) Self-disciplined and organised (iii) Quiet and shy.

Fill in the blanks. (a) The seven Cs of oral communication include clear, concise, complete, correct, concrete, courteous and ________. (b) A group of 5 to 12 employees from the same department is a ________ team.
questions.answer: (a) Candid. (b) Problem-solving.

questions.q: True or False. (a) A virtual team uses computer technology to tie together dispersed members. (b) Heredity alone fixes personality at birth.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: environment and situation also shape it.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain any two principles of effective writing.
questions.answer: Unity: sentences, paragraphs and the whole message should deal with one idea. Coherence: relation and clarity among sentences, so the message is clear.

questions.q: Explain the importance of communication in the tourism industry.
questions.answer: Managers cannot plan, organise, lead and control without it. Tourism is a service industry where staff spend most of their time communicating with customers.

or.q: Explain two main objectives of a meeting.
or.answer: To inform and explain information to members, and to get feedback and exchange ideas. Meetings also persuade members to accept change and resolve conflicts.

questions.q: Mention any two features of communication.
questions.answer: It involves at least two persons, a sender and a receiver. It is incomplete without feedback and aims at creating understanding.

or.q: Mention any two advantages of oral communication.
or.answer: It provides immediate feedback and gives a chance for dialogue. It is fast, economical and flexible.

questions.q: Examine any two disadvantages of written communication.
questions.answer: It is time-consuming and costly and gives no immediate feedback. It is rigid and impersonal, and secrecy is hard to maintain.

questions.q: Elucidate the four stages of team development.
questions.answer: Forming: members are cautious and explore. Storming: conflict about goals and roles surfaces. Norming: members agree on decision-making and standards. Performing: the team works together to get results.

questions.q: Distinguish between introverts and extroverts.
questions.answer: Extroverts are sociable and assertive and feel energised by being with people. Introverts are quiet and shy and feel recharged by being alone.

or.answer: Team building is a formal activity to improve the development and functioning of a team. It helps reshape norms and strengthens cohesiveness.

questions.q: Describe two advantages of written communication.
questions.answer: It is taken more seriously and provides a record for reference. It is suitable for long messages and can reach many people at once.

questions.q: Explain 'information overload as a barrier to communication'.
questions.answer: It means receiving a huge number of messages at one time, such as a hotel receptionist getting over 20 calls in five minutes. The receiver cannot attend to them all.

questions.q: Explain 'coherence' as a principle of effective writing.
questions.answer: Coherence means relation and clarity among the parts of the writing. It applies to sentences, paragraphs and the whole message.

questions.q: Explain 'situation' as a determinant of personality.
questions.answer: The specific situation a person meets shapes personality, such as a job interview or a picnic. Pleasant or unpleasant experiences change traits.

questions.q: Explain agreeableness as a personality trait.
questions.answer: It is the tendency to be compassionate and cooperative rather than suspicious. It also measures how trusting, helpful and well-tempered a person is.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the three steps in the process of convening a meeting.
questions.answer: (i) Notice: it tells members the date, time, place and issue. (ii) Agenda: a list of topics to be discussed, sent to members. (iii) Minutes: the decisions and conclusions recorded after discussion.

questions.q: Distinguish between oral and written communication (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Oral messages are spoken and quick; written messages take time. (ii) Oral gives immediate feedback but no record; written gives a record and reference. (iii) Oral suits short messages and secrecy; written suits long messages and is precise.

questions.q: Explain the seven Cs of written communication (three of them with meaning).
questions.answer: (i) Clarity: a clear objective and simple words. (ii) Completeness and conciseness: answer what, who, when, why and where briefly. (iii) Courtesy, consideration, correctness and concreteness: friendly 'you-attitude', correct facts and specific statements.

questions.q: How should a tourism professional handle customer complaints? (three points)
questions.answer: (i) Listen sympathetically, stay calm and do not take it personally. (ii) Record the details and deal with written complaints at once. (iii) Offer repair, replacement or refund, follow up and report back with a solution.

questions.q: Explain the personality traits of the Big Five model (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Openness to experience and conscientiousness (creative and curious; disciplined, organised). (ii) Extroversion and agreeableness (sociable; compassionate and cooperative). (iii) Emotional stability: the degree of control over unpleasant emotions.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the role of written communication in tourism in six points.
questions.answer: (i) It is taken seriously and provides records. (ii) It suits long messages such as itineraries and brochures. (iii) It gives clear guidelines for staff and tourists. (iv) It reaches many persons at once. (v) Letters, memos, reports and manuals make business accurate. (vi) The seven Cs make it effective and correct format keeps it professional.

or.q: Explain the steps for building an effective team.
or.answer: (i) Consider every member's ideas valuable. (ii) Be aware of unspoken feelings and communicate clearly. (iii) Encourage trust, cooperation and information sharing. (iv) Delegate problem-solving and facilitate communication. (v) Set a clear goal and ground rules. (vi) Establish a method for consensus and encourage listening and brainstorming.

questions.q: How to face an interview? Explain in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Plan and rehearse with a friend. (ii) Be in control: introduce yourself and shake hands first. (iii) Minimise distractions such as the phone. (iv) Keep eye contact to look confident. (v) Frame answers positively and avoid jargon. (vi) Never speculate; if you do not know, say so and promise to find out.

questions.q: Explain the process of communication and the barriers to it, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) The sender has a message. (ii) Encoding turns it into symbols. (iii) The channel carries it to the receiver. (iv) The receiver decodes it. (v) Feedback completes the process. (vi) Barriers are noise, distance, information overload, language and an unfamiliar medium.

questions.q: Explain customer care management in six points.
questions.answer: (i) It is the system to maximise customer satisfaction. (ii) Understand needs and match products to them. (iii) Give value for money and reliable service. (iv) Gather feedback and keep customers informed. (v) Use loyalty schemes such as discounts and cards. (vi) Handle complaints courteously, sympathetically and swiftly.
